key_insight: The paper proposes label-free hidden-cohort fairness, which improves model fairness by optimizing performance across latent appearance-based patient groups rather than only visible demographics.
clinical_relevance: This could make medical imaging models more equitable and robust across underrepresented or unseen subgroups, without requiring demographic labels during training.
method: Cluster images into K appearance-based hidden cohorts using visual features.
Apply fairness optimization across these latent cohorts instead of single demographic attributes.
Evaluate whether this reduces disparities on both single and multiple demographic axes.
evidence_signal: Using the HIDFairBench benchmark, the method reportedly achieved state-of-the-art fairness on single and multiple demographic attributes even though demographic labels were not used for training.
watch_item: Appearance-based clusters may not align cleanly with clinically meaningful subgroups, so cohort selection and validation will be important before deployment.
paper_title: Fairness Beyond Demographics: Optimizing Performance Across Appearance-Based Hidden Cohorts in Medical Imaging
